entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gnaeus Manlius Cincinnatus was the first of the patrician gens Manlia to obtain the consulship, which he held in 480 BC, together with Marcus Fabius Vibulanus. His father's name was Publius.

Cincinnatus's rise to consulship was marked by his leadership during the Latin War, a conflict with the neighboring city-state of Veii, which he helped bring to an end through his strategic military campaigns.

As consul, Cincinnatus's primary focus was on addressing the growing economic and social tensions within Rome, implementing policies aimed at reducing inequality and promoting the welfare of the common people.

Cincinnatus's legacy extends far beyond his own lifetime, as he set an important precedent for future Roman leaders and helped establish the foundation for the development of the Roman Republic.

"The Roman people always remembered Cincinnatus with gratitude and reverence," writes the Roman historian Livy, "for he was the first of our fathers to have been called to the consulship, and his integrity and wisdom were beyond compare."
